reports.category: Fake Return Scams: Secure Your Crypto Investments
reports.description: I became victim to a scam through a fraudulent investment website called i-ox.com, which was introduced to me by individuals who built trust via a Discord connection.After chatting for about three weeks with a Man who claimed to be a crypto trader, he introduced me to someone he referred to as her “Teacher.” He invited me to trade cryptocurrencies using their platform. Initially, everything seemed legitimate—I saw small returns on my investments. Later, he persuaded me to invest a larger amount, citing a supposed “ event” with promised returns of 100%.In total, I transferred 100,000 USDC through 4 separate transactions from my Binance account to various wallet addresses. Shortly after, my account was allegedly frozen due to claims of insider trading. I was told to deposit an additional $30,000 as “insurance” to unlock my funds. Following that, they continued to demand more payments for things like taxes in the UK and Ireland, as well as other fabricated fees—adding up to another $20,000+. lost everything and felt like my life was over. I was in a very dark place, but I got it all back by filling a complaint through the support center of westtech via "westtech online" support centre on Whtspp via ‪+1 (763) 406‑2089‬

reports.description: After having problems on buying a NFT on zonic.app, I have joined the discord on their site. After that, I was taken to another smaller server, and I was calmly reporting my situation. After that they told me I need to fix something using a site they provided, and connect my wallet. But they dont had walletconnect, they are just listing every wallet, and are asking for seed phrase/private key/json. After raising my suspicion to the 'support', they tried to convince me that it is safe because of the https certificate. Thanks to my 7 year web developement experience, I know that this certificate has nothing to do with the site itself, putted in 'fjdhkf' as my seed phrase, inspected the network and saw two POST methods, sending my text to their private database, so they could have my seedphrase if I were dumb enough. After that I got told things like 'fuck off', and got kicked out from the server and I have no proof for the chat. But still, you can look everything up on the site I provided, its obvious, try out to replicate my situation for proof. The bitcoin address I provided is a random one, because I only wanted to report the site in itself and i have no address from the scammers. Im sure many people got scammed like this, because it is going from zonic, a legit marketplace where i still found my nft and got it.
